title: Spire and Thorn Again
premise: Tamsin Sterling has survived three years in the city of Vell by hiding his beast-speaker gift beneath a shopkeeper's smile, selling harmless charms in a realm where magic is outlawed and its practitioners burned. When a mute child arrives at his door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Tamsin learns he is the last heir of an ancient covenant between humans and the wild thorn-realm of the Spire — a covenant his own family helped break. Hunted by the Inquisitor General and betrayed by the friend who sold him out years ago, Tamsin must carry the child to the Spire's heart before the dying pact collapses entirely, unleashing the feral old magic it once contained. He succeeds only by sacrificing his hidden life: he speaks the truth of his gift aloud in the city square, accepting exile so that the reforged covenant can bind both realms into an uneasy, honest peace.
about_author: Edmund Fairweather is the pen name of a former field botanist who spent a decade cataloguing hedgerows across northern moorlands before turning to fantasy. His work is known for its tactile naturalism, morally tangled loyalties, and animals who are never quite what they seem.

chapters.title: The Charm Shop at Winter's Edge
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We meet him selling luck-knots and mended-bone charms in occupied Vell, carefully magicless, while a caged wren whispers warnings he pretends not to hear. Establishes his double life and quiet loneliness. Emotional beat: the ache of a gift smothered for survival.

chapters.title: A Knock in Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A mud-caked boy of about eight appears at his door during a curfew storm, speaking syllables no human throat should know — and every animal in the street goes silent. The wren names the boy 'Hollowroot.' Emotional beat: dread and recognition colliding; Tamsin's cover is already cracking.

chapters.title: What the Rats Remember
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Using beasts as reluctant informants, Tamsin learns the boy fled the Spire's collapse three nights ago and that something is hunting him through the sewers. First glimpse of the Inquisitor General's hounds, which smell magic like blood. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Inquisitor General Maren Vale's POV. Vale interrogates a charm-seller down the street with terrifying politeness, revealing she has a list of suspected practitioners — and Sterling is second from the top. She keeps a thorn splinter in a glass case that moves on its own. Emotional beat: cold, patient menace.

chapters.title: Three Years of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with flashbacks. We learn how Tamsin escaped the purge that killed his mother, and how his childhood friend Dace Corrow testified against the coven to save himself — and now serves Vale. Emotional beat: guilt over survival; loyalty and truth beginning their war.

chapters.title: The Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The wren reveals she was once a covenant-warden bound to Tamsin's bloodline, and that the boy Hollowroot is not a child at all but the Spire's last seed wearing a child's shape. To restore the covenant, Tamsin must carry him to the Spire's heart within one moon. Emotional beat: awe curdling into terror at the scale of the ask.

chapters.title: Burning the Shop
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. With Vale's hounds closing in, Tamsin torches his own shop to erase evidence and flees the city walls with Hollowroot hidden in a fish cart. Dace spots him leaving and says nothing — yet. Emotional beat: grief for the small safe life, deliberately destroyed.

chapters.title: Road Through the Ashfields
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On the road north, Hollowroot begins speaking more, and the land around him greens unnaturally fast — fields bloom, wolves gather without attacking. Tamsin realizes the boy's presence is already changing the balance. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by the knowledge that miracles draw hunters.

chapters.title: The Toll-Keeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: New character POV: Brannoc, a bridge toll-keeper whose daughter was taken by the old magic years ago. He shelters Tamsin and Hollowroot, then betrays their route to Vale in exchange for a promise about his daughter. Emotional beat: compassion and betrayal entwined; everyone pays for survival.

chapters.title: Hounds of Honest Law
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. Vale pursues, but her conviction wavers when her lead hound kneels to Hollowroot instead of attacking. She executes the hound for disobedience and hardens herself further. Emotional beat: the cost of a truth-denying ideology, shown from inside the antagonist.

chapters.title: Dace at the Ford
chapters.summary: Dace's POV. Dace intercepts Tamsin at a river ford, ostensibly to arrest him, actually to beg him to surrender quietly — Vale will be merciful, he swears. Old friendship resurfaces; Tamsin refuses, naming Dace's testimony as the wound it was. They part as enemies. Emotional beat: heartbreak disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Thornwalk
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Guided by the wren, they enter the Thornwalk, a forest that predates kingdoms, where trees remember names and test travelers with their own memories. Tamsin relives his mother's burning and nearly turns back; Hollowroot holds his hand through it. Emotional beat: confronting inherited trauma head-on.

chapters.title: The Herd That Waits
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The Thornwalk's great stags convene a judgment: they blame humanity for breaking the covenant and want Hollowroot returned to die with it. Tamsin, the first beast-speaker in a generation, argues their case — not with apology, but with proof he listens. Emotional beat: earning trust rather than inheriting it.

chapters.title: Halfway to the Heart
chapters.summary: Alternating brief POVs. Vale's column burns the Thornwalk's edge; Dace falters watching it; Brannoc's daughter is found alive inside the fire line, changed. The realms' damage becomes visible to all sides. Emotional beat: escalation and dawning complicity.

chapters.title: The Splinter Speaks
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. The captive thorn splinter finally speaks to Vale — in her dead sister's voice — offering to return everything the purge took if she lets the covenant die. Vale, shaken, rides faster toward the Spire. Emotional beat: temptation aimed precisely at a wound.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate of Roots
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the Spire's outer gate, Dace catches them again — but this time he's brought Vale's whole column, having traded Tamsin's location for a pardon. Hollowroot is seized; the wren is killed shielding Tamsin. Emotional beat: the lowest point; loyalty weaponized against love.

chapters.title: The Seed and the Sword
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, captive. In Vale's camp, Hollowroot begins to wilt without the Spire's soil, and Tamsin understands the boy will die within days. He makes Vale an offer: witness the truth of the covenant herself before destroying it. Emotional beat: desperate bargaining, dignity intact.

chapters.title: What Vale Buried
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. Inside the Spire's threshold, the old magic shows Vale her own past — how the purge she serves began with her sister's death by feral magic, and how the covenant's collapse will unleash far worse. Her certainty cracks. Emotional beat: an antagonist choosing between vengeance and truth.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the Spire's heart, Tamsin plants Hollowroot in the last living soil, but the rite demands a speaker willing to be bound — voice, name, and future — to both realms. Dace, arriving unbidden, takes the binding blow meant to kill Tamsin, redeeming his betrayal at fatal cost. Emotional beat: sacrifice answering sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Square at Dawn
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The covenant restored, Tamsin returns to Vell to end the hunt: he stands in the market square and speaks openly with every animal present, declaring his gift before the city. Vale, bound by what she witnessed, formally ends the purges rather than deny the truth she saw. Emotional beat: truth chosen over safety at last.

chapters.title: Green Over Broken Stone
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Weeks later: Vell adapts uneasily to a world where hedge-witches practice openly and the Thornwalk's edge creeps toward the walls. Brannoc reunites with his changed daughter, who remembers the Spire fondly. Emotional beat: cautious, imperfect hope taking root.

chapters.title: Spire and Thorn Again
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. A year on, Tamsin tends a new shop at the Thornwalk's edge — charms still, but honest ones — while a young sapling called Hollowroot grows tall beside the door, learning to speak in both tongues. The wren's descendants nest in his eaves. Emotional beat: quiet homecoming; inheritance transformed from burden into gift.
